raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fix tensor-to-NumPy conversion in audio input parsing and shared multimodal hashing.

Following @DarkLight1337's suggestion, I checked the other explicit conversion paths and confirmed the same gradient-related failure in multimodal hashing.

## Claims

- Handle CUDA and gradient-tracking audio tensors by detaching and moving them to CPU before NumPy conversion.
- Detach tensors before hashing, covering image/video tensors and precomputed audio embeddings.
- Add regression coverage and document direct audio Tensor inputs.

## Validation

Before the fixes, the audio model test and the three CPU hashing cases failed with:

```text
RuntimeError: Can't call numpy() on Tensor that requires grad.
```

After the fixes:

| Environment | Validation | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS, CPU | Full parser and hasher suites | 57 passed, 4 skipped |
| DGX Spark, CPU/CUDA | New hashing regression for image, video, and audio embeddings | 6 passed |
| DGX Spark | Full parser suite | 34 passed |
| DGX Spark | Whisper Tiny `LLM.generate()` regression | 1 passed |

The hashing tests verify exact hash equality with detached reference tensors.

The Whisper test uses real weights and the `mary_had_lamb` audio sample. It compares gradient-tracking CPU tensors, CUDA tensors, and gradient-tracking CUDA tensors with a NumPy reference using `check_logprobs_close`.

Image/video and embedding coverage exercises parsing and hashing; the real-model test covers raw audio.

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

Local parser and hasher suites:

```sh
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' \
  ../vllm-dev/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/multimodal/test_parse.py \
  tests/multimodal/test_hasher.py -q --tb=short
```

The new hashing regression was run before and after changing the hasher:

```sh
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' \
  ../vllm-dev/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/multimodal/test_parse.py::test_hash_parsed_tensor_with_grad \
  -q --tb=short
```

Before: `3 failed, 3 skipped`. After: `3 passed, 3 skipped`.

DGX CUDA coverage:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/audio-tensor-fix/worktree:/tmp/audio-tensor-fix/testdeps \
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=ERROR \
/home/matrix/vllm-venv/bin/python -m pytest \
tests/multimodal/test_parse.py::test_hash_parsed_tensor_with_grad \
-v -s --tb=short
```

DGX model regression:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/audio-tensor-fix/worktree:/tmp/audio-tensor-fix/testdeps \
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=ERROR \
/home/matrix/vllm-venv/bin/python -m pytest \
tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_whisper.py::test_audio_tensor_inputs \
-m core_model -q -s --tb=short
```

</details>

All applicable pre-commit hooks, test tethering, and `git diff --check` passed.

## Details

Audio parsing previously called `.numpy()` directly, which fails for CUDA tensors and tensors requiring gradients.

The shared multimodal hasher already moved tensors to CPU, but did not detach them before calling `.numpy()`. Adding `detach()` fixes gradient-tracking inputs while preserving the hashes produced for their detached equivalents.

The DGX validation used this branch's Python source with installed vLLM 0.31.0 native extensions. Startup reported missing Triton kernels and unavailable FlashInfer sampling, but Whisper inference completed. These tests validate input compatibility, not model accuracy.

The earlier search of open PRs found no matching audio conversion fix.

AI assistance was used.

---

<details>
<summary>Pull Request Checklist</summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Keeps the fixes at the existing audio conversion and shared hashing boundaries.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Includes before/after regression evidence, CPU/CUDA coverage, and real-model audio validation.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Applicable pre-commit hooks passed, and audio input documentation was updated.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes the root causes, validation results, and environment limitations.

</details>

@@ -379,6 +379,11 @@ vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct \
 
 You can pass a tuple `(array, sampling_rate)` to the `'audio'` field of the multi-modal dictionary.
 
+You can also pass a one-dimensional `torch.Tensor` directly. vLLM detaches
+the tensor, moves it to CPU, and converts it to a NumPy array before audio
+processing, so tensors on CUDA devices and tensors with `requires_grad=True`
+are supported.
+
 Full example: [examples/generate/multimodal/audio_language_offline.py](../../examples/generate/multimodal/audio_language_offline.py)
 
 #### Chunking Long Audio for Transcription

@@ -127,6 +127,50 @@ def check_model_available(model: str) -> None:
     model_info.check_transformers_version(on_fail="skip")
 
 
+@pytest.mark.core_model
+def test_audio_tensor_inputs(vllm_runner: type[VllmRunner]) -> None:
+    audio, sample_rate = AudioAsset("mary_had_lamb").audio_and_sample_rate
+    if sample_rate != WHISPER_SAMPLE_RATE:
+        audio = AudioResampler(target_sr=WHISPER_SAMPLE_RATE).resample(
+            audio, orig_sr=sample_rate
+        )
+
+    with vllm_runner(
+        "openai/whisper-tiny",
+        dtype="half",
+        max_model_len=448,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=2048,
+        max_num_seqs=1,
+        enforce_eager=True,
+        enable_prefix_caching=False,
+        mm_processor_cache_gb=0,
+    ) as vllm_model:
+        reference = vllm_model.generate_greedy_logprobs(
+            [VLLM_PROMPT], 16, num_logprobs=5, audios=[audio]
+        )
+        assert reference[0][0]
+
+        audio_tensor = torch.as_tensor(audio)
+        audio_cases = {
+            "CPU with gradients": audio_tensor.requires_grad_(True),
+            "CUDA": audio_tensor.detach().to("cuda"),
+            "CUDA with gradients": audio_tensor.detach()
+            .to("cuda")
+            .requires_grad_(True),
+        }
+        for name, tensor in audio_cases.items():
+            result = vllm_model.generate_greedy_logprobs(
+                [VLLM_PROMPT], 16, num_logprobs=5, audios=[tensor]
+            )
+            assert result[0][0]
+            check_logprobs_close(
+                outputs_0_lst=reference,
+                outputs_1_lst=result,
+                name_0="NumPy",
+                name_1=name,
+            )
+
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("requires_grad", [False, True])
+def test_parse_audio_tensor_detaches_before_numpy(requires_grad):
+    """Audio tensors are accepted even when they require gradients."""
+    parser = MultiModalDataParser()
+    audio = torch.tensor([0.1, 0.2], requires_grad=requires_grad)
+
+    items = parser.parse_mm_data({"audio": audio})["audio"]
+
+    np.testing.assert_array_equal(items.get(0), audio.detach().numpy())
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "modality,shape",
+    [
+        ("image", (3, 8, 8)),
+        ("video", (2, 8, 8, 3)),
+        ("audio", (1, 4, 8)),
+    ],
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("device", ["cpu", "cuda"])
+def test_hash_parsed_tensor_with_grad(modality, shape, device):
+    """Image, video, and embedding tensors remain hashable with gradients."""
+    if device == "cuda" and not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        pytest.skip("Requires CUDA")
+
+    tensor = torch.arange(np.prod(shape), device=device).reshape(shape).float()
+    tensor.requires_grad_()
+    data = {modality: [tensor]} if modality == "image" else {modality: tensor}
+    items = MultiModalDataParser().parse_mm_data(data)[modality]
+    item = items.get_all_items_for_hash()[0]
+    assert isinstance(item, torch.Tensor)
+
+    actual = MultiModalHasher.hash_kwargs("blake3", **{modality: item})
+    expected = MultiModalHasher.hash_kwargs("blake3", **{modality: item.detach()})
+
+    assert actual == expected
+
